In the event that a Lender becomes a Defaulting Lender and the other Lenders have not confirmed to the New Borrower within five Banking Days of receiving the notice referred to above that they will honour the commitment of any Defaulting Lender, no commitment fee shall be payable to the Facility Agent for the account of that Defaulting Lender on any unused portion of the Maximum Loan Amount of that Defaulting Lender for any day on which that Lender was a Defaulting Lender. documents referred to in part 1.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Other laws</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:6.05pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">4.7</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">No law of any jurisdiction other than England has any bearing on the opinion contained in part 2.</font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:6.05pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:51.84pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:64.08pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:6.05pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:4.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;text-indent:-29.45pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">5</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.78pt">Qualifications</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">This opinion is subject to the following qualifications&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Contractual matters</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">The enforcement of contractual obligations is subject to the general principles of contractual liability, in particular the matters described in the following paragraphs.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">Apart from claims for the payment of debts (including the repayment of loans), contractual obligations are normally enforced by an award of damages for the loss suffered as a result of a breach of contract&#59; and recoverable loss is restricted by principles such as causation, remoteness and mitigation. The specific performance of contractual obligations is a discretionary remedy and is only available in limited circumstances.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.3</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">Contractual obligations can be discharged by matters such as breach of contract or frustration. Claims may become time-barred or may be subject to defences such as set-off or estoppel.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.75pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.4</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">The interpretation of the meaning and legal effect of any particular provision of a contract is a matter of judgment, which will ultimately be determined by the relevant tribunal. In addition, a document may be capable of being rectified if it does not express the common intention of the parties.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.5</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">English law has traditionally been protective of guarantors and has developed a number of defences for them. Although guarantees generally purport to exclude many of these  defences, a guarantee, and any third party security generally, will be construed in favour of the guarantor or grantor of security where possible.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.6</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">A clause in a contract which excludes or limits an obligation of one of the parties or the liability for breach of that obligation will be construed restrictively, against the person who wishes to rely on it.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.7</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">If a provision of a contract is particularly one-sided it is more likely to be construed against the party who wishes to rely on it.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:6pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.8</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">A provision of a contract may be ineffective if it is incomplete or uncertain or provides for a matter to be determined by future agreement.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:6pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.9</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">A provision of a contract which provides for the conclusive certification or determination of a matter by one party may not prevent judicial inquiry into the merits of the claim.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.10</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">Although the parties to commercial contracts are generally free to agree what they want, this principle does have limits. For instance, a provision for the payment of a sum in the event of  a breach of contract is unenforceable if it is a penalty, and a provision which prevents the assignment of a receivable may be ineffective.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.11</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">A contractual provision for the forfeiture of a proprietary or possessory interest, such as the rights of a lessee under a chattel lease, may be overridden.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;text-indent:-42.05pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.12</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.6pt">An undertaking to assume liability for stamp duty or similar taxes may be ineffective.</font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;text-indent:-42.05pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:51.84pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:64.08pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;text-indent:-42.05pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:3.9pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.13</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">As a general principle, an authority or power of attorney can be revoked at any time, and will be revoked if the donor enters into insolvency proceedings. This is so even if the authority or power is expressed to be irrevocable and the revocation is therefore made in breach of contract. The main exception to this principle is where the authority or power is granted as part of a security arrangement.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.14</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">A provision of a contract which purports to exclude the effect of prior or subsequent agreements, representations or waivers may be ineffective.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.15</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">A provision of a contract which provides what will happen in the event of an illegality (including a provision for severance of part of the contract) may not be enforceable.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;text-indent:-42.05pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.16</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.6pt">An agreement in respect of criminal liability may not be enforceable.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;text-indent:-42.05pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.17</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.6pt">An indemnity for the costs of litigation may not be enforceable.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:24.6pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Security</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.35pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42.15pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.18</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.7pt">We express no opinion on the priority of the security created by the English Security Document in relation to any other rights affecting the assets which are the subject of the security, whether those rights are absolute or by way of security, whether they are created by agreement or arise by operation of law and whether they are created before or after the English Security Document. In relation to particular types of asset, further steps may be required (such as effecting registrations or giving notices) to protect the priority of security against claims by third parties.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.19</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">To the extent that the English Security Document purports to create a legal (as opposed to an equitable) interest, there are limits on the availability of such an interest and further steps may be required (such as, in relation to land, registration at H.M. Land Registry) in order to create one.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.20</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">The assets which are the subject of a security created by the English Security Document may consist of rights against third parties, such as contractual rights. To the extent that they do, the security is subject to the terms of those rights (which may, for instance, prohibit the creation of security) and may be subject to the rights of those third parties (who may, for instance, have rights of set-off).</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.21</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">We express no opinion on the effect of the English Security Document to the extent that it relates to assets which are situated or registered outside England or are governed by a law other than English law.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.22</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">A purported fixed charge over an asset will be treated as floating security if the chargee has insufficient control over it and its proceeds.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.23</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">The rights of the holder of floating security over assets to the net proceeds of those assets  are subject to the payment of various other liabilities including preferential debts, certain unsecured debts and the expenses of certain insolvency proceedings.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.24</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">As a general principle, a creditor with security over the whole (or substantially the whole) of the assets of a company cannot appoint an administrative receiver of the company but, instead, can appoint an administrator.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.25</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">A receiver ceases to be the agent of the company over whose assets he has been appointed once that company goes into liquidation.</font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:51.84pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:64.08pt;width:100%"><div><font><br></font></div><div><font><br></font></div></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:3.9pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.26</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">A provision of the English Security Document may be ineffective to the extent that it purports to limit a Company&#8217;s right to the return of the charged assets once it has repaid the secured obligations.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Insolvency</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.27</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">The parties&#8217; rights are subject to laws affecting creditors&#8217; rights generally, such as those relating to insolvency and reorganisation. These laws can apply to persons incorporated or resident outside England, as well as to those incorporated or resident in England.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;text-indent:-42.05pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.28</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.6pt">In particular, on an insolvency&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.35pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(a)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.13pt">contractual and other personal rights will reduce proportionately with all similar rights, and contractual provisions which would conflict with this principle (such as a pro rata sharing clause) are ineffective&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.35pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(b)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.13pt">transactions (including the security created by the English Security Document) entered into in the period before the insolvency starts (that period generally being no longer than two years) may be set aside in certain circumstances&#59; and</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.35pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(c)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.69pt">the ability of a secured creditor to enforce its security may be subject to limitations, for instance in an administration or moratorium.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Choice of law and jurisdiction</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:6.15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.29</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">The law which governs a contract and any connected non-contractual obligations is not determinative of all issues which arise in connection with that contract. For instance&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.35pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(a)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.13pt">it may not be relevant to the determination of proprietary issues (such as those relating to security)&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.35pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(b)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.13pt">rules which are mandatory (which includes public policy rules) in a jurisdiction which is connected with the contract or in the jurisdiction where the issue is decided may be applied regardless of the provisions of the contract&#59; and</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.35pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(c)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.69pt">in insolvency proceedings, the law governing those proceedings may override the law governing the contract.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.30</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">There are circumstances in which the English courts may, or must, decline jurisdiction or stay proceedings. Additionally, it may not be possible to commence proceedings because of an inability to comply with service of process requirements.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:6pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.31</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">The English courts have a discretion to accept jurisdiction in an appropriate case even though there is an agreement that other courts have (exclusive or non-exclusive) jurisdiction.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.85pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.32</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">The jurisdiction of the English courts in relation to insolvency matters is not dependent on the submission of the parties to the jurisdiction. The precise scope of that jurisdiction depends on the nature of the insolvency procedure in question.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">Sanctions</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.33</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">Any provision of a contract which requires a party to comply with the sanctions-related legislation of a foreign jurisdiction may be unenforceable and unlawful.</font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.9pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:51.84pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div Policy.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font to exercise its mission of provider of public services (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">mission de service public</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">), such assets and the title of Bpifrance Assurance Export thereto may be immune from suit or execution&#59; and</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.35pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(c)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.69pt">suit and execution against Bpifrance Assurance Export&#8217;s assets or properties may be affected by action taken by the French Republic authorities in the interests of national defence or on the occurrence of exceptional circumstances of paramount importance to the national interest of the French Republic, as such concept is understood under the Constitution, laws and regulations of the French Republic.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.15pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42.15pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">2.11</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.7pt">While there is no express waiver by the French State of immunity from jurisdiction set forth in the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy, we are of the opinion that &#91;Article 20&#93; of the General Terms and Conditions- Credit Institutions &#91;(ASC EC 17-01)&#93; (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Conditions G&#233;n&#233;rales &#8211; Etablissements de Cr&#233;dit</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">) applicable to the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy, by providing that any disputes that may arise in connection with the application of the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy shall be submitted to the jurisdiction of the relevant courts in Paris, constitutes an implied and valid waiver of any such immunity from jurisdiction. The language employed in such Article 20 provides that &#8220;Any disputes that may arise in connection with the application of the policy shall be submitted to the jurisdiction of the relevant courts in Paris&#8221; without specifying whether the general judicial courts or the administrative courts are the competent courts. While there is to our knowledge no definitive answer to such question, we are of the view that the judicial courts (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">ordre judiciaire</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">) would be the competent courts. This is based both on our prior experience and on the fact that, although the French State is the party responsible for payment under the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy, it has designated Bpifrance Assurance Export, which is a commercial company, to act as its agent for the purposes of administering the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy. The French State is normally represented by the </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Agent judiciaire de l&#8217;Etat </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">before relevant courts of Paris (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">ordre judiciaire</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">).</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42.15pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">2.12</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.7pt">Under the laws of the French Republic, the French State is subject to French public law and benefits from sovereign immunity over its property or assets, within the meaning of the relevant administrative case law (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">jurisprudence administrative</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code G&#233;n&#233;ral de Propri&#233;t&#233; des Personnes Publiques</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">).</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.3pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font Insurance Policy will not violate, conflict or exceed (i) Bpifrance Assurance Export&#8217;s or the French State&#8217;s powers or statute, or (ii) any provision of applicable law or regulation to which Bpifrance Assurance Export or the French State is subject.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div Export Insurance Policy is effective and would be recognised and upheld as a valid choice of law by the French courts.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div Policy by means of an &#8220;Adobe Acrobate Reader process&#8221; signature or a &#8220;copy-pasted&#8221; signature on the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy together with an accompanying note attached to the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy confirming that Bpifrance Assurance Export has validly and conscientiously signed the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy and agreed that by this signature, Bpifrance Assurance Export intents to be bound by the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy will be considered by a French court as a satisfactory evidence of the agreement of the parties to the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy. The question as to whether it can be evidenced that a document has been validly entered into between parties is question of fact. Evidence of such a fact may be provided with a &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">commencement de preuve par &#233;crit</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8221; (written evidence) as defined within article 1362 of French Code Civil. Whether a document constitutes a &#8220;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">commencement de preuve par &#233;crit</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">&#8221; is a question of fact which may ultimately be assessed and decided by a French court. We note however, that a French court may also take into consideration that pursuant to article 1358 of French Code Civil and article L.110-3 of the French Commercial Code, in a commercial transaction between commercial parties (as is the case with the entry into the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy), the mode of evidence that an agreement has been validly entered into is free.</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font Code (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code des assurances</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">) do not apply to such Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy and that it is instead subject to general contract law (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">le droit commun des contrats</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">). Consequently, we express no opinion as to whether it constitutes &#34;insurance&#34; in accordance with the French Insurance Code. However, we reiterate our opinion in paragraph 2.6 as to the legal, valid, binding and enforceable effect of the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:4.95pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.2</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">the exercise of rights under the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy is subject to satisfaction of all relevant conditions of effectiveness under the terms thereof and to compliance by the beneficiary with such rights of its own obligations as set forth in such Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy, and failure to comply with such obligations may entitle the French State in certain circumstances to be released from its obligation to indemnify for the losses covered therein vis-&#224;-vis such beneficiary&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.3</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">the Background Documents are not conclusive about the status of Bpifrance Assurance Export. For example, the </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Registre du Commerce et des Soci&#233;t&#233;s </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(Registry of Commerce and Companies) is reliant on third parties to provide them with information&#59; and there will be a time-lag between the occurrence of an event (such as insolvency) and its notification to, and subsequent appearance at, the Registry of Commerce and Companies. Additionally, the Registry of Commerce and Companies does not exhaustively record all material events which may affect a company (however, this would not affect the status of the French State as the entity responsible for the cover provided under the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy)&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.4</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">the enforcement of the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy may be limited by applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, or similar arrangements, or by moratorium or other laws relating to or affecting the enforcement of creditors' rights generally insofar as it is issued by Bpifrance Assurance Export&#59; however, we point out in this respect that Bpifrance Assurance Export is in this instance acting on behalf, in the name and under the control of the French State and that&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.8pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(a)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.58pt">pursuant to Article L. 432-4 of the French Insurance Code, Bpifrance Assurance Export acting on behalf, in the name and under the control of the French State establishes a separate and distinct accounting for transactions which it concludes with the guarantee of the French State&#59; and</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.8pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">(b)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:16.58pt">in accordance with Articles L. 432-1 and L. 432-2 of the French Insurance Code, the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy constitutes direct obligations of the French State&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.5</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">a French court has the power under article 1343-5 of the French Civil Code (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code civil</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">) to postpone or spread over time the payment of the sums due for a period not in excess of two years, taking into account the situation of the debtor and the needs of the creditor. In such case, the court may also provide separately that any payments which are postponed will bear interest at a reduced rate (but not less than the legal minimum rate), or that payments will initially be allocated to principal rather than interest. The court may require as a condition to such decision that the debtor accomplish certain acts in order to facilitate or guarantee the payment of the debt. A decision of a court made pursuant to article 1343-5 of the French Civil Code (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code civil</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">) suspends any procedures for enforcement which have been commenced by the creditor, and any default interest or penalties incurred due to late payments cease to be due during the period fixed by the court. Any contractual stipulation to the contrary will not be effective. Article 1343-5 of the French Civil Code (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code civil</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">) is a rule of general application and therefore will probably apply to Bpifrance Assurance Export, as a private company, since there is no specific exception provided by law or decision of the French courts in relation to article 1343-5 of the French Civil Code (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code civil</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">). However, the position of the French State, as the direct obligor in respect of the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy, would in our view not qualify for rescheduling of the debts&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.55pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.6</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">the enforcement under French law or before a French court of provisions of any of the Operative Documents concerning damages and indemnification could be limited by application of all or part of the provisions of articles 1231 </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">et seq</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">. of the French Civil Code (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code civil</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">) pertaining to damages and indemnification in contractual matters (in particular, but without limitation, article 1231-5 of the French Civil Code (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code civil</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">), under which,</font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="height:54pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div such amount in proportion to the benefit which such partial performance conferred on the beneficiary of the obligation)&#59;</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div However, if a judgement awarded by a French court were to be expressed in Euro, it would normally be expressed by reference to the exchange value of the relevant amount of the said foreign currency at the rate of exchange prevailing on the date of the judgement or, if the court so decides at the claimant's request, at the actual date of payment&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-36.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.8</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.61pt">in the event of any proceedings being brought in a French court in respect of a monetary obligation expressed to be payable in a currency other than euros, a French court would probably give judgement expressed as an order to pay, not such currency, but its euro equivalent at the time of payment or enforcement of judgement. With respect to a bankruptcy, insolvency, liquidation, moratorium, reorganisation, reconstruction or similar proceedings, French law may require that all claims or debts be converted into euros at an exchange rate determined by the court at a date related thereto, such as the date of commencement of a winding-up&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div arbitrary basis or not to have been given or made in good faith&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div English language and not in their original French terms, such translations may not comprehensively cover the meaning of such legal concepts under French law. This opinion may, therefore, only be relied upon under the express condition that any issues of interpretation arising thereunder will be governed by French law and be brought before a French court&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.45pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;text-indent:-42.05pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.13</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.6pt">other than as set out in paragraph  2.17, we do not express any opinion as to any taxation matters&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.14</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">our opinion as to the enforceability of the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy relates only to its enforceability under French law in circumstances where the competent French court has and accepts jurisdiction&#59; the term &#34;enforceable&#34; refers to the legal character of the obligations assumed by the parties under such Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy, i.e. that it is of a character which French law generally enforces or recognises&#59; furthermore, and with respect to the Bpifrance Assurance Export Insurance Policy which is expressed to be governed by French law, pursuant to the French Civil Code (</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Code civil</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">), the reliance on or the enforcement of contractual terms and conditions may under certain circumstances be contrary to an overriding principle of good faith or to the principle that rights must not be exercised unreasonably (principle of </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">abus de droit</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">) &#59; and this opinion is based upon the laws, and published judicial and administrative decisions as of the date hereof, which are subject to any amendment, repeal or other modification of the applicable laws or judicial or administrative decisions hereafter enacted or rendered, and</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:47.3pt;padding-right:5.2pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-42pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">5.15</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;padding-left:22.55pt">the law which governs a contract and any connected non-contractual obligations is not determinative of all issues which arise in connection with that contract. For instance&#58;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.4pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="margin-top:0.05pt;padding-left:75.6pt;padding-right:5.25pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-28.8pt"><font ownership of, or security granted over, such asset&#59;</font></div><div style="margin-top:0.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div
